## Corpora

| Corpus | What it is | In the repository |
|---|---|---|
| UDHR | The Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 47 languages, the usual corpus for comparing Unicode compression schemes, since the same content exists in many languages | Yes |
| Mixed content | 23 hand-written files that mix scripts as real data does: chat with emoji, technical text with English words, JSON, HTML, typographic punctuation | Yes |
| Names and UI strings | Names of people and places, titles and UI strings, one per line | Yes |
| Wikipedia | 388 articles on eight topics in 56 languages, fetched on 2026-11-20 | No: the text is under CC BY-SA, so the tool fetches it |

The tool normalizes all text to NFC and trims the lines. The text is then cut into values in several ways, and **each value is encoded on its own**, as a database stores a field:

| Values | How they are made |
|---|---|
| 4-, 8- and 16-character values | Each paragraph cut into pieces of at most that many UTF-16 code units, without splitting a surrogate pair |
| Paragraphs | Each paragraph (line) a value |
| Documents, articles | Each whole file, or each Wikipedia article, a value |
| Mixed lines, names and UI strings | Each line a value |

Short values show what a key or a short field costs, where the first character of each value pays for the change of script. Documents show what long stored text costs.

## Codecs of the Size Tables

| Codec | What it is | Keeps code point order |
|---|---|---|
| **Steno** | The Steno Encoding | Yes |
| UTF-8, UTF-16 | The Unicode encodings | UTF-8 yes; UTF-16 only without supplementary characters, such as emoji |
| SCSU, BOCU-1 | ICU's converters | SCSU no; BOCU-1 yes |
| Deflate fast and max, Brotli 1 and 11, LZ4 fast and max, Zstd 1 and 19 | UTF-8, then the compressor at that level, on each value by itself | No |

Sizes are counted bytes, and they are the same on every machine. Every codec decoded every value back to its text, which the tool checks.

#### SCSU Sizes Depend on the Encoder

SCSU leaves choices to the encoder, and the choices change the size. The sizes here are those of ICU's encoder; another SCSU encoder can give other sizes for the same text.

#### Compressors Work on Each Value Alone

The compressors compress each value by itself, with nothing shared between values, as a database that compresses each field would. On short values they are larger than UTF-8. On long documents they are the smallest by far. What a compressed value gives up is what the Steno Encoding is for: its bytes do not sort, a prefix of the text is not a prefix of the bytes, and another compressor version or level can give other bytes for the same text.

## Regenerating the Numbers

The sizes come from the benchmark tool in `Source/dotnet/Singulink.Steno.Benchmarks`; its [README](https://github.com/Singulink/Steno/blob/main/Source/dotnet/Singulink.Steno.Benchmarks/README.md) says how to fetch the Wikipedia corpus and run the report. SCSU and BOCU-1 come from the `icu.dll` of Windows 10 1903 and later; on other systems the tool leaves them out. The speeds come from the benchmarks of each implementation, each run on its own on a quiet machine; the README of each implementation names the command. The tool then writes every fragment and chart of this section into `Docs/benchmarks` from the result files alone, and the measurements stay in [Docs/benchmarks/data](https://github.com/Singulink/Steno/tree/main/Docs/benchmarks/data) and in the `bench` folder of each implementation.
